messages:
Alyssa: FYI pushed gpu-base:2026.03 to us-west-2/eu-west-1 nodepools. Immediately seeing ~30% of GPU pods CrashLoopBackOff with native driver lib errors.
Ben: Which errors? paste pod output and the image's toolkit version.
Alyssa: Pod log snippet from inference-a-2:

nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: nvml: library not found: libnvidia-ml.so.1
error: mounting "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1" into container rootfs: no such file or directory

Image manifest shows: "nvidia-container-toolkit": "2.0.0" and we stripped driver artifacts to shrink the layer (used "cuda-drivers:latest" meta).
Carol: Sounds like we removed the host-compat symlinks or changed ld cache paths. Containers are expecting host-mounted libs but image changes mean runtime can't resolve nvml.
Ben: On a node, run these checks and paste results:

ssh node-456
ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu | grep nvidia
ldconfig -p | grep libnvidia-ml
journalctl -u kubelet -n 200

We need to determine if the host has drivers and whether containers relied on in-image libs.
Alyssa: Host output (node-456):

lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 20 Mar 16 11:02 libnvidia-ml.so.1 -> libnvidia-ml.so.535.86.10
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 1.1M Mar 16 11:02 libnvidia-ml.so.535.86.10

But in the container image we removed those files, so the mount path inside the container didn't exist even after the bind.
Fran: infra-bot reports nodepool flapping in eu-west-1 since 11:05 UTC. We're losing capacity and some Dedicated customers are impacted.
Dave: Customer impact: roughly 35-45% GPU capacity in affected regions offline; autoscaler spun up replacement on-demand nodes, ~+$3k/day burn. Need immediate triage + mitigation path.
Ben: Short-term options:
- Roll back gpu-base image to 2026.02 for affected nodepools (fast, needs drain)
- Restore driver libs into image (slower rebuild)
- Restart nvidia runtime on nodes (unlikely to fix missing files)
I recommend rollback node image to 2026.02 and cordon+drain a few nodes for faster recovery.
Carol: Add CI preflight to the image pipeline: run an actual GPU container test like `docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.7-base nvidia-smi` and fail if nvml errors.
Alyssa: Rolling back us-west-2 now. Commands:

gcloud compute instance-templates set-instance-template --instance-template gpu-base:2026.02 --zone us-west-2a
# then terraform apply to trigger nodegroup rolling update

I'll leave one affected node unscheduled for deep-debug.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260316-1143 created and assigned to Alyssa+Ben. Severity P2.
Alyssa: +15m update: us-west rollback finished, pods recovered (~96% back). EU rollback queued.
Fran: Note: Dedicated customers got failed-over to Hosted but saw latency spike. Sales alerted by one APAC customer.
Dave: Action items (owners): rollback EU (Alyssa), CI preflight (Carol), pin toolkit in build (Ben), update runbook re: libcuda mounts (Fran). Also track cost impact in postmortem.
Ben: Longer term: stop stripping driver libs unless we ship a compatibility shim. Build an image-level compatibility check that validates host-bind paths and lib names.
Carol: Adding a canary promotion for base images (10% nodepools for 1 hour) so future rollouts are limited.
Alyssa: EU rollback complete. Incident resolved. I'll draft postmortem and include timeline + cost estimate.
Ben: Opening INFRA ticket to pin toolkit and add preflight test. Also check whether upstream apt package names changed which could have broken our slim step.
infra-bot: Created INFRA-9123 to pin toolkit and enforce preflight.
Alyssa: Saved failing container stacktrace at /var/tmp/gpu-failure-node-456.log and node debug dump at /var/tmp/node-456-debug.tar.gz
Carol: CI preflight job added and turned mandatory. :white_check_mark:
Fran: Postmortem will include detection time, mitigation time, affected capacity, customer impact, and cost delta. Please update this thread with any customer escalations.
Ben: Thanks team. We'll follow up with the postmortem doc and corrective PRs.
